body.en: You're putting together your household's emergency plan for flood season. You can only tackle one piece first. Which gives you the most protection?

choices.label: Agree on a meeting point and who grabs the emergency documents, water, and medicine bag if you have to leave fast
choices.consequence: Right priority. Most harm during a fast-moving flood comes from confusion in the first few minutes — a clear plan for where to go and who grabs what removes that confusion before it costs you time.

choices.label: Buy an expensive emergency kit and figure out the rest later
choices.consequence: Backwards order. A kit is useless if nobody agreed on the plan around it — coordination matters more than equipment as the first step.

choices.label: Assume everyone will know what to do when it actually happens
choices.consequence: This is exactly what emergency plans exist to prevent. Under real pressure, people default to panic, not instinct — a plan discussed calmly beforehand is what actually gets followed.
